criteria.text: `compare(base, cand, ['graph'])` returns `kept: true` for a candidate whose targeted cells return the same hashes but are slower than the base (e.g. 100 ms -> 300 ms), and the returned object has no `slow` key; `Verdict` has no `fast` field.

`compare` still returns `kept: false` when any comparable cell's hash differs, when a targeted cell is missing, when no targeted cell exists, and (with `strict = true`) when any base cell is missing from the candidate.
`table()` still prints the `new / base` ratio column.
`compare.ts` rejects no candidate on speed: running it on two reports with identical hashes and a 3x slower candidate exits 0 and its verdict line contains no percentage.

`renderCases(queries, ctx, allNames)` against the fixture's persons returns one entry per name in `readCases` plus `linksFast`, `compareFast`, `lensesFast`, and each entry's text equals the text the same `queries.*` builder renders for that ctx (no drift from what routes send).

Every rendered case, wrapped by `explainOf`, executes against the in-memory fixture database (after `buildGraphAggregates`) and its output contains `Execution Time:`; `summarize` on that output returns a finite `executionMs`.

`summarize` on a canned plan containing `Batches: 16`, `Sort Method: external merge  Disk: 51232kB` and `Rows Removed by Join Filter: 1843220` returns all three lines in `flagged`, and does not flag `Batches: 1` or `Sort Method: quicksort`.

`summarize` on a canned plan with `Buffers: shared hit=120 read=88, temp read=40 written=41` on the top node and other `Buffers:` lines on children returns exactly `sharedHit 120, sharedRead 88, tempRead 40, tempWritten 41`; a plan with no `Buffers:` line returns zeros.

`run` against a recording fake client sends only statements matching `^(begin transaction read only|rollback|explain \(analyze, buffers, format text\) |select )`; no statement matches `\b(set|reset|insert|update|delete|create|drop|alter|analyze|vacuum|truncate)\b` at its start, and no `pg_stat_statements_reset`.
`run` sends each case's explain exactly twice, each inside its own `begin transaction read only` ... `rollback` pair, and labels them `cold` then `warm` in the report.
When the fake client rejects the `pg_stat_statements` select, `run` still produces every case's section, the report contains "pg_stat_statements indisponível", and the result's failure flag is false.
When the fake client rejects one case's explain, the report shows that case's error, the following cases still run, `rollback` is sent for the failed case, and the result's failure flag is true.
`run` with an unknown `--cases` name, or an unknown `--person`, sends no explain and reports the valid names/ids.
`inBuildWindow` is true at 06:17, 06:59 and 07:01 UTC, false at 06:16, 07:02 and 09:30 UTC; `run` with a date inside the window and `force: false` sends no statement.
A person with no docs in the window (fixture person, `days` before every doc) renders every case with `ids = []` without throwing.
`test/` never opens a network connection for this script: the tests use the fixture's PGlite or a fake client only (no `POSTGRES_URL*`/`DATABASE_URL` read in the test process).

The docs state, as facts: the PGlite harness proves identical rows and plan shape and is not a timing source; production `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and `pg_stat_statements` are the only timing source of truth; the two reasons (PGlite keeps temp files in RAM where production spills past `work_mem`, and PGlite's whole database fits in memory where production's does not fit `shared_buffers`); how to run `prod-explain.ts`, that it is read-only, needs `PG_SSL_CA`, and must run outside the build window. Checked against `test/docs.ts`'s `docsText` (e.g. `prod-explain` and `pg_stat_statements` both appear, and the text near them mentions `work_mem` and `shared_buffers`). `test/docs-drift.test.ts` covers collectors only and does not cover this.

`scripts/bench/README.md` no longer describes a speed gain as a condition for keeping a candidate (no `--gain` flag in its flag table). (This page is outside `docsText`; checked by reading the file's flag table in a test or manually.)
